[Messages]
[systems]: This case concerns a dispute under a multi-year supply agreement between Alpha Components (supplier) and Northbridge Medical Systems (buyer). The disputed issues include: (1) whether Northbridge breached a volume commitment clause by reducing orders in the last two quarters; (2) whether Alpha failed to meet agreed delivery schedules and quality specifications during the same period; and (3) what payment, credit, or adjustment is owed as a result. Please review the parties' initial statements below.

[SupplierRepresentative]: Thank you for taking the time to review this matter.

Alpha Components entered into a three-year supply agreement with Northbridge Medical Systems on 1 March 2023 to provide custom-assembled controller boards. The contract includes a minimum annual volume commitment of 24,000 units (2,000 units per month on average), with pricing set on the assumption that this volume would be met.

From March 2023 through January 2024, Northbridge's purchase orders consistently met or exceeded the agreed monthly average. Beginning in February 2024, however, Northbridge sharply reduced orders, placing only 800 units in February, 600 in March, and 500 in April. No force majeure or other contractual justification was invoked. We attach a spreadsheet of all POs and our corresponding delivery confirmations.

Alpha scaled production capacity and component purchases to meet the contract volumes. Based on Northbridge's sudden reduction, we are now holding approximately $1.4M in inventory and dedicated capacity that was committed in reliance on the agreement. Under Section 4.2 (Volume Commitment and Shortfall Payments), Northbridge is obligated to compensate Alpha for the margin on the shortfall relative to the annual minimum.

Northbridge has refused to pay the calculated shortfall invoice of $1.05M issued on 15 May 2024. They have instead asserted generalized concerns about delivery timing and a small number of quality issues. Our records show that (a) on-time delivery performance remained above 96% against the agreed delivery windows, and (b) out of over 20,000 units delivered, only 73 units were returned for rework, all of which were replaced within 10 business days at no cost to Northbridge, consistent with Section 6.1 (Remedies for Nonconforming Goods).

We are requesting that the platform confirm Northbridge's obligation to pay the shortfall invoice of $1.05M and to continue ordering at the contracted minimum volumes for the remainder of the term, or, alternatively, to pay the early-termination fee specified in Section 9.3. We are, of course, willing to provide full documentation of orders, deliveries, and communications as needed.

[BuyerRepresentative]: Thank you for the opportunity to present Northbridge Medical Systems' position.

We do not agree that Northbridge is in breach of the agreement. While the contract contains a volume commitment, it must be read together with Alpha Components' obligations to meet our delivery timelines and quality requirements, which are critical in a regulated medical-device context.

Beginning in November 2023, we started experiencing recurring delays on several key POs. For example, PO #NB-231108 for 2,400 units, requested for delivery by 15 December 2023, arrived in three partial shipments, with the final 600 units delivered on 12 January 2024. Similar slippage occurred with PO #NB-240102 and PO #NB-240215. We have attached an internal log showing these dates and the impact on our production schedules.

In addition, we observed a noticeable uptick in quality issues starting in early 2024. While Alpha did replace or rework affected units, the disruptions forced us to rework our own manufacturing plans and hold extra safety stock. This directly undermines the assumptions behind the original volume commitment, which was premised on reliable just-in-time deliveries.

Given these ongoing concerns, and after several discussions with Alpha, we made a considered decision to reduce orders and qualify an alternate supplier. We believe this was a commercially reasonable response to Alpha's performance issues. We also question the size of the claimed shortfall amount: Alpha's $1.05M invoice appears to assume full margin on volumes we never actually ordered, without properly netting the costs and delays we incurred.

Northbridge is prepared to pay for all conforming product actually received and to discuss a reasonable accommodation that reflects both sides' contributions to the current situation. However, we do not accept that we owe the full shortfall or that we must continue to order at prior levels regardless of Alpha's performance. We request that the platform review the delivery and quality records and determine a fair allocation of responsibility and any appropriate adjustment.
